summary: The study describes the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to coat polysilicon micro-mirrors with an Al2O3/W multilayer to enhance x-ray reflectivity at 1.54 Å wavelength. The ALD process involves alternating layers of Al2O3 and W, with specific precursor gases used for each layer. The coating reduces the snap-down voltage and maintains the mechanical functionality of the micromirrors.
evidence: The micro-mirror array is coated using atomic layer deposition with an Al2O3/W multilayer. The precursors for W ALD were tungsten hexafluoride (WF6) and disilane (Si2H6). The precursors for Al2O3 ALD were trimethylaluminum (Al(CH3)3) and water (H2O). The ALD process was carried out at 125°C. The snap-down voltage was reduced by half after coating.
